vectors.description: an inception with three next weights for two next key digests
vectors.reason: a weighted threshold has exactly one weight per key digest ("Three weights mean there MUST be exactly three corresponding key pairs")

vectors.description: inception with nt="2" and two next key digests; a rotation with k=[K1,K1] and kt="1", signed twice by K1 (index 0 and index 1, both with prior-next index 0). Only one pre-rotated key is exposed
vectors.reason: one exposed pre-rotated key counted twice does not satisfy a prior next threshold of two keys; a key list must not repeat a key
vectors.spec_quote: To establish verifiable rotation control authority, the current key list MUST include a satisfiable subset of exposed (unblinded) pre-rotated next keys from the most recent prior Establishment event. Where satisfiable concerns the prior next threshold.

vectors.description: inception and rotation (kt=1 of 2) signed by K2; the identical rotation again with K3's signature; then a different interaction at s=1 with only a random signature

duplicity.note: neither the re-sent rotation (same SAID) nor the unverified interaction is a verified different version of an event at s=1, so neither is evidence of duplicity. Keeping K3's late signature on the accepted rotation is keripy behaviour; the specification does not require it.

vectors.reason: a duplicitous event is a verified but different version of an event at the same location; an identical event is not duplicitous and an unverified one is dropped
vectors.spec_quote: A duplicitous event is defined as a verified but different version of an event at the same location.

vectors.description: inception with c=["RB"], b=[B1], bt=1 and a=[] (no registrar backer seal for B1), signed and receipted by B1
vectors.reason: with RB the establishment event must include a registrar backer seal for each backer
vectors.spec_section: Configuration traits field / Registrar Backer seal
vectors.spec_quote: The `Registrar-Backer`, `RB` config trait indicates that the [[ref: Backer]] (witness) list in the establishment event in which this trait appears provides the AIDs of ledger registrar backers. The event MUST also include Registrar Backer Seal for each registrar backer in the list.

vectors.description: a delegator with a transferable basic prefix whose inception anchors the seal of a delegated inception; the delegated inception's source seal couple points at that inception (s=0)
vectors.reason: any event of the delegator that carries the event seal can be the delegating event
vectors.spec_quote: A delegating event is a type of event that includes in its data payload an event seal of the delegated event that is the target the delegation operation.

keripy.note: keripy refuses a source seal couple with s=0: validateDelegation validates the couple's sequence number with inceptive=False (src/keri/core/eventing.py:3279), so an anchor in the delegator's inception is found only by its KEL search, when no source seal is attached (see the no-source-seal variant)

vectors.description: inception with b=[W1,W2], bt=1 (witnessed); a rotation with br=[], ba=[W1], bt=1, controller-signed and signed by W1 at index 0
vectors.reason: ba entries already in the backer list are skipped; the witness list stays [W1,W2]
vectors.spec_quote: Given such an event, the current backer list is updated by appending in order the AIDs from the Backer Add, `ba` list except for any AIDs that already appear in the current Backer list.
vectors.ambiguity: The specification says to skip AIDs of ba that are already witnesses, keripy refuses the event and keriox appends W1 again: three behaviours, so interop needs a decision. The expected outcome follows the specification text.

vectors.description: inception with b=[W1,W2], bt=1 (witnessed); a rotation with br=[W9] (not a witness), ba=[], bt=1, controller-signed and witnessed by W1
vectors.reason: removing an AID that is not in the list leaves the list unchanged
vectors.spec_section: Backer remove list / Backer add list
vectors.spec_quote: The AIDs in the Backer Remove, `br` list MUST be removed before any AIDs in the Backer Add, `ba` list are appended.
vectors.ambiguity: The specification does not say what happens when br names an AID that is not a witness. Removing it is a no-op under the literal reading; keripy refuses the event.

vectors.description: inception with b=[W1,W2], bt=1 (witnessed); a rotation with br=[W1], ba=[W1], bt=1, controller-signed and witnessed by W2 at index 0; an interaction witnessed by W1 at index 1 (W1's position after remove-then-append, [W2,W1])
vectors.reason: br is applied before ba, so W1 is removed and appended again
vectors.spec_section: Backer remove list / Backer add list
vectors.spec_quote: The AIDs in the Backer Remove, `br` list MUST be removed before any AIDs in the Backer Add, `ba` list are appended.
vectors.ambiguity: "except for any AIDs that already appear in the current Backer list" can mean the list before the event (W1 is skipped, giving [W2]) or the list after removal (giving [W2,W1]); keripy refuses any overlap. Witness-indexed signatures resolve to different keys under each reading. The expected outcome follows the literal remove-then-append reading.

vectors.description: inception with b=[W1,W2] and bt=0, controller-signed, no witness signatures
vectors.spec_quote: The [[ref: Backer]] threshold, `bt` field value is a hex-encoded non-negative integer. This is the number of backers in the backer list that MUST support a key event for it to be valid.
vectors.ambiguity: The specification allows any non-negative integer bt and a threshold of 0 is met by no receipts; keripy requires 1 <= bt <= len(b) whenever b is not empty.

vectors.description: an accepted inception and interaction; a different interaction at s=1 with a random controller signature
vectors.reason: an event without a verified signature is dropped; it is not evidence of duplicity
vectors.spec_quote: A duplicitous event is defined as a verified but different version of an event at the same location.

vectors.description: the same key state notice with a.s="10" (sn 10 written in decimal, which reads as hex 0x10 = 16) and d the SAID of the sn-10 event
vectors.reason: there is no event at sn 0x10; the notice is inconsistent with the KEL
vectors.spec_section: KERI field labels (s: Sequence Number). The spec does not define the /ksn route itself, so this rests on the generic s rule and on keripy interop
vectors.spec_quote: |`s`| Sequence Number | strictly monotonically increasing integer encoded in hex |

keripy.note: keripy accepts it: processReplyKeyStateNotice compares d with the KEL only when it has an event at the notice's sn (src/keri/core/eventing.py:5317-5326), and there is none at 0x10

vectors.description: a /loc/scheme reply of eid B (Ed25519) whose receipt couple carries B with B's valid Ed25519 signature bytes coded 0C (ECDSA secp256k1)
vectors.reason: the signature does not verify against the key; the reply is rejected (a validator must not crash)
vectors.spec_quote: Confirm signature on the Update verifies against indicated key-state under which signature was made.

keripy.note: keripy verifies the signature bytes with the key's algorithm and ignores the signature code (Cigar.verfer.verify), so it accepts the reply
